primary_question: At fixed candidate pool, support size, presentation budget and training seed, does a preregistered selection rule improve the four-benchmark mean or reduce lower-tail risk relative to uniform random support draws?

common_rules.replication_policy: screen every method and support size once with selection seed 42 and training seed 42; add support or training replicates only after the complete first-pass matrix is available
common_rules.selection_cost_unit: GPU-hours measured from selection-job wall time times allocated GPUs; CPU-only selection is reported as 0 GPU-hours with CPU time retained separately
common_rules.training_budget_match: same optimizer steps, batch size and balanced number of prompt presentations within each setting
common_rules.uncertainty: task-level bootstrap for benchmark scores; support-seed distribution shown without treating three draws as proof of equivalence

methods.uniform_random: PCG64 permutation of the exact candidate pool; take a nested M=8 then M=48 prefix without replacement
methods.stratified_random: proportional source and prompt-length strata, plus frozen pretraining difficulty strata where that field exists; random within strata
methods.semantic_diversity: normalized Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B prompt embeddings; deterministic farthest-first traversal initialized at the candidate nearest the global centroid
methods.hard_selection: lowest initial-student pass rate under a frozen K=8 rollout per candidate; deterministic hash tie break
methods.shortest: lowest mean generated response length under the same frozen K=8 initial-student rollout
methods.cost_d_opt: existing reliability-aware gradient sketch and cost-aware greedy D-opt implementation, extended from M=8 to M=48 without changing its score definition

justrl_deepmath.candidate_pool: existing frozen 384-candidate reliability/SVD cohort selected independently before method outcomes
justrl_deepmath.endpoint_policy: all primary JustRL/DeepSeek selection endpoints are retrained from the same initial student for exactly 65 optimizer steps; prior 100-step endpoints are external controls only
justrl_deepmath.primary_table_warning: The full-pool uniform M8 and candidate3840 stratified M48 are external controls, not matched entries in the candidate384 six-method table.

code_eurus.external_control: historical M1/M48/M3840/full endpoints at step 100 use the same teacher-student pair and downstream Code evaluation protocol
code_eurus.endpoint_policy: all primary Code selection endpoints use 100 optimizer steps. The earlier 50-step screen is retained as an intermediate checkpoint only: Eurus-dev peaked near step 50, but that in-pool n=2 curve does not establish convergence of HumanEval+, MBPP+, or LiveCodeBench, while all historical approximately-60-point Code references were evaluated at step 100

qwen30b_deepmath.source_pool: the frozen DeepMath 3840 cohort used by the completed stratified M48 arm
qwen30b_deepmath.external_control: historical stratified M48 step-15 endpoint is an external control only
qwen30b_deepmath.endpoint_policy: all primary 30B-to-4B M48 selection endpoints use 25 optimizer steps; two independent step-25 pilot trajectories still reduced on-policy k1 by about 19-22% from step 15 and changed the two-AIME validation mean from 0.533 to 0.542 and from 0.500 to 0.533, respectively
